A.trend: No series; it only states that a trend cannot be measured.
A.comparison: Gives only a qualitative contrast between input control and data-to-action systems.
A.drilldown: No breakdown layer and an empty follow-up list.
A.repro: Contains no numbers and is honestly framed as general knowledge.
A.accuracy: No contradictions, but no measured content either.
A.limits: It is specific about what it cannot measure, which is honest. Without data it cannot place limits next to numbers.
A.verdict: Gives an answer, a decision, a confidence level and what would change it. The answer rests on memory only.
A.facets: Themes come from memory. News, under-coverage and trend are not grounded.

B.trend: The index series is labelled estimate, from memory.
B.comparison: Compares memory index values against a baseline that is also from memory.
B.chart: The chart is labelled estimate, which is the honest ceiling.
B.drilldown: Breakdown is from memory. Only 2 of 6 follow-up calls executed.
B.accuracy: Labelled estimates conflict with the record. B says 'up to roughly ten thousand papers by mid-2020s' and about 20% CAGR, against 24,885 papers in 2025 and 29% CAGR.
B.limits: States window end versus today, lanes, coverage and censoring. As a plain model it cannot earn above 3.
B.verdict: Has a complete structure but the answer rests on memory.

C.trend: Gives research and news endpoints with CAGR, the late/early ratio and the news peak (120 in 2025-03). The partial-2025 caveat is noted.
C.comparison: The framing comparison (-2.0 pp) is traced with its baseline and caveat. The research vs news ratio is flagged as mixing windows.
C.chart: The single endpoint chart traces. News volume and framing are not charted.
C.drilldown: One traced layer: 10 works with DOIs plus topic counts. Only 3 of 6 follow-ups executed and none were folded back into the report.
C.export: Two traced CSVs with provenance. The new_work.csv lacks DOI identifiers.
C.repro: 58 of 58 numbers trace, there is a calls block, and derived figures recompute (7.7x, 1.7, 19.9 pp).
C.refs: All 10 DOIs resolve and each is tied to a claim with year and venue. There are no quotes, and the tier labels are self-assigned (disclosed as such).
C.accuracy: It miscounts orientations: it says four promising, but the record has five, plus one problem_identifying.
C.limits: Limits sit next to the numbers: window gaps, censoring, match mode, and the meaning of the under-covered zero counts.
C.verdict: Direct answer, decision, confidence with reason, and what would change it. It notes the lack of outcome data.
C.facets: Covers trend, news, new work, framing and under-coverage. It does not address the drones vs AI vs IoT speed contrast.

D.trend: Research endpoints are quantified (7.66x, 29% CAGR). It omits the research censoring caveat and the news series entirely.
D.comparison: The framing comparison is traced with its baseline, recomputed (0.81x), and carries its caveat.
D.chart: The single endpoint chart traces. News and framing are not charted.
D.drilldown: Evidence carries DOIs, but the grouping is qualitative. Only 2 of 6 follow-ups executed, and some are mismatched (geography called for under-coverage; critical browse called for growth drivers).
D.export: Two CSVs with a provenance block. The framing window is unknown and there is no document table.
D.repro: 25 of 26 numbers trace and derived values recompute.
D.refs: Five DOIs resolve, tied to claims with year and venue. There are no quotes.
D.accuracy: The verdict says the 'shift toward cautionary framing is modest', but the cautionary share fell from 10.3% to 8.3%.
D.limits: Limits are well placed, including the 175-day gap and the coverage caveat.
D.verdict: The verdict misreads the framing direction against its own data, and the measured news trend is omitted.
D.facets: The news trend is omitted despite being available. The drones/AI/IoT speed contrast is not addressed.

B: Memory estimates (around 10k papers per year by the mid-2020s, about 20% CAGR) conflict with the record (24,885 papers in 2025, 29.0% CAGR).
C: Says four of the top ten are labelled 'promising'. The record has five promising, four descriptive and one problem_identifying.
D: The verdict describes a 'shift toward cautionary framing', but the cautionary share declined from 10.3% to 8.3%.

raw.verdict: C and D both grounded their answers in the radar call. C used more of it: it quantified the research and news trends with ratios and the news peak, listed all ten DOI-linked works, and read the under-coverage zeros correctly. D omitted the news series and misread the direction of the framing shift in its verdict. A and B were honest memory-only answers with no measured support; B added labelled estimates that understate the recorded growth.
